cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's just poured out his heart over his own people, Israel (Romans 9:2-4). Now he asks, "What then will we say?"
His answer starts with the Gentiles, who weren't pursuing righteousness at all. No jogging, no stretching, didn't even BUY the shoes.

cards.question: The Gentiles, who didn't pursue righteousness, have obtained it anyway.
What kind of righteousness did the Gentiles obtain?

cards.text: Then there's Israel, and Israel WAS chasing. They pursued a law of righteousness.

cards.question: Paul says Israel attained the righteousness they were chasing.

cards.text: So Paul asks the question we're all thinking: "Why not?"

cards.question: Why didn't Israel attain the righteousness they were chasing?

answers.text: They pursued it as if by works
They pursued it without the law

cards.text: They stumbled over the stumbling stone. All that running, and they TRIP.
Paul backs it up with Isaiah, a prophet (Isaiah 8:14; 28:16). The lines speak of a stone laid in Zion, a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.

cards.question: Paul quotes Isaiah about a stumbling stone in Zion. What does the quote say about the one who believes in Him?

answers.text: They will never be put to shame

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal. He calls his readers brothers and opens up about his own people.

cards.question: Paul says his heart's desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their ___.

cards.text: And Paul vouches for them: they're zealous for God. ALL in.

cards.question: Paul says Israel's zeal for God is based on knowledge.

cards.text: They were ignorant of God's righteousness and sought to establish their own. I tossed the recipe to invent my own dough ONCE, and the smoke alarm still brings it up.

cards.question: Israel tried to set up their own righteousness. What does Paul say they did not do with God's righteousness?
Paul writes that someone is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes. Who is it?

cards.text: Now Paul puts two kinds of righteousness side by side. For the kind that's by the law, Moses, Israel's leader, writes (Leviticus 18:5): "The man who does these things will live by them."

cards.question: The righteousness by faith says not to ask in your heart who will ascend into heaven. Paul says that would be to do what?

cards.text: Same goes the other way: don't ask who will descend into the Abyss to bring Christ up from the dead.

cards.question: The righteousness by faith says not to ask who will go up to heaven or down to the Abyss. What does it say about the word instead?

cards.text: The faith lines Paul just quoted echo Moses (Deuteronomy 30:12-14). Paul calls this "the word of faith we are proclaiming" and lays it out plain.

cards.question: Paul says if you confess with your ___ that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your ___ that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.

cards.text: With your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved. Then Paul quotes Isaiah again (Isaiah 28:16): "Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame."

cards.question: Paul says there's a difference between Jew and Greek.
The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives ___ to all who call on Him.

cards.text: Paul quotes Scripture: "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." EVERYONE, friend. No velvet rope, no "sorry, we're at capacity."

cards.question: Paul works backward: how can they call on the One they haven't believed, or believe in the One they haven't heard? And how can they hear without what?
Next in Paul's chain: how can they preach unless they are ___?

cards.text: Paul quotes Isaiah (Isaiah 52:7): "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!"

cards.question: Paul says everyone the good news was brought to welcomed it.

cards.text: Isaiah even asks (Isaiah 53:1), "Lord, who has believed our message?" I bet that question stung.

cards.question: Paul sums up his chain. How does he say faith comes?

answers.text: By hearing the word of Christ
By keeping the law of Moses

cards.text: Paul asks whether those who didn't welcome the good news never heard it. Indeed they did, he says, quoting Psalm 19:4: "Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world." That's the whole PLANET on reply-all.
Then Paul asks, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says (Deuteronomy 32:21): "I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding."

cards.question: Isaiah boldly says the One speaking was found by those who did not seek Him.
As for Israel, the next line speaks of a disobedient and obstinate people. What does the One speaking say He has been doing toward them all day long?

answers.text: Holding out His hands to them
Turning His face away from them
